title: 第 45 課｜正則變換：座標與動量可以互換｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
廣義座標的選擇本來就沒有任何限制，只要能唯一決定系統的位置就好。換到另外一組獨立的量，拉格朗日方程的形式完全不變，這種變換叫做點變換。既然拉格朗日方程不變，哈密頓方程當然也不變；但哈密頓的寫法其實允許更廣的變換，因為在這裡動量和座標是地位平等的獨立變數。所以我們可以把全部二倍 s 個變數一起換掉：新的座標和新的動量都同時依賴舊的座標和舊的動量，這種自由度是哈密頓寫法的一大好處。不過並不是所有這種變換都保持正則的形式。哈密頓方程可以由最小作用量原理導出，變分對座標和動量各自獨立進行；新變數若也滿足哈密頓方程，同樣的原理也必須成立。兩個形式要等價，只要它們的被積函數相差某個函數的全微分就行，因為差別只是端點上的常數，不影響變分。滿足這個條件的變換就叫正則變換，那個函數叫生成函數。把關係式整理一下就能直接讀出係數：舊動量是生成函數對舊座標的偏導數，新動量是它對新座標的偏導數再取負號，而新舊哈密頓量差一個對時間的偏導數。有時候用舊座標和新動量當自變數比較方便，做一次勒讓德變換就得到另一個生成函數，這時舊動量是它對舊座標的偏導數，新座標是它對新動量的偏導數。無論用哪一種，新舊哈密頓量的差永遠是生成函數對時間的偏導數，所以生成函數不顯含時間時，新哈密頓量就是把舊的直接換成新變數。正則變換的範圍這麼廣，座標和動量的區別幾乎只剩下名字：取新座標等於舊動量、新動量等於負的舊座標，就只是把兩者對調而已，所以一般就叫它們正則共軛量。最後，帕松括號在正則變換下不變，於是正則的條件可以用基本括號乾淨地寫出來；而系統隨時間的演化本身，也是一連串的正則變換。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 45 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 45 | Canonical Transformations: Coordinates and Momenta May Trade Places | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
The choice of generalised coordinates is subject to no restriction: they may be any quantities that fix the position of the system. Passing to any other independent set leaves the form of Lagrange's equations unchanged, and such a change is called a point transformation. Since Lagrange's equations are unchanged, Hamilton's equations are unchanged too, but the Hamiltonian treatment in fact allows a much wider range of transformations, because there the momenta are variables independent of and on an equal footing with the coordinates. So all two s of the variables may be transformed together: the new coordinates and the new momenta may each depend on the old coordinates and the old momenta, and this enlargement is one of the important advantages of the treatment. Not every such transformation keeps the equations in canonical form, however. Hamilton's equations follow from the principle of least action with coordinates and momenta varied independently, and if the new variables also obey them, the same principle must hold in the new variables. The two forms are equivalent if their integrands differ by the total differential of some function, since the difference is then a constant fixed at the endpoints, which cannot affect the variation. Such a transformation is called canonical, and that function is its generating function. Rearranging the relation lets the coefficients be read off directly: the old momentum is the derivative of the generating function by the old coordinate, the new momentum is minus its derivative by the new coordinate, and the two Hamiltonians differ by its time derivative. Sometimes the old coordinates and the new momenta are the more convenient variables; one Legendre transformation gives a second generating function, whose derivative by the old coordinate is the old momentum and whose derivative by the new momentum is the new coordinate. Whichever form is used, the difference of the two Hamiltonians is always the partial derivative of the generating function with respect to time, so if it does not contain the time, the new Hamiltonian is the old one with the new variables substituted. The range of these transformations is so wide that the distinction between coordinates and momenta is little more than a name: one of them simply interchanges the two, which is why they are called canonically conjugate quantities. Finally, Poisson brackets are invariant under canonical transformations, so the canonical condition can be written cleanly through the fundamental brackets, and the evolution of the system in time is itself a chain of such transformations.

Lesson 45 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
